summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old male with a history of systolic heart failure (EF 35%), interstitial lung disease, COPD, lung cancer after Cyberknife therapy, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea over three days. Initial evaluation revealed elevated proBNP and engorged pulmonary vessels on chest imaging, consistent with mild volume overload. Despite no significant weight gain or leg swelling, his symptoms were attributed to acute on chronic heart failure, poorly tolerated due to underlying lung disease. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to increased oral torsemide (60 mg daily) and started on lisinopril 2.5 mg daily. Abdominal discomfort was evaluated with CT, which ruled out acute pathology and suggested chronic constipation. His condition improved, he was able to lie flat, and was discharged home after two days. He was advised to continue home medications, use nicotine patch for smoking cessation, monitor weight daily, and follow up with cardiology, pulmonology, and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung, unspecified
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
